purpose: Mechanism H exploratory test: HYDE_QUERY_REFORMULATION, Campaign V2's second candidate after Mechanism G's DROP.
excludes_note: all 55 units used or examined anywhere in this arena to date (49 pre-Campaign-V2 + the 6 fresh units from second-hop-expansion-v1). _abs variants excluded by base id too.

inputs_never_used: the $0 absence/precondition checks performed on OTHER already-examined units
selection_rule.method: deterministic: 1 unit per LongMemEval-S category (6 categories), first-by-question_id-sort within category after exclusion. Unweighted -- HyDE's target precondition (question/fact phrasing mismatch) is architecturally universal per LongMemEval's own construction methodology, not category-gated, so no category is up-weighted.
selection_rule.size_note: 6 units, matching Mechanism G's exploratory scale (contract preference <$0.50 per mechanism before replication).

precondition_evidence: See docs/research/HYDE_QUERY_REFORMULATION_V1.md for the full $0 diagnostic: across all 11 BASE-wrong units observed project-wide to date, 9/11 were retrieval-absence failures (not 'evidence present but misread', the precondition CoVe/RARR/self-consistency-style mechanisms need). A direct full-store dump (memory.get_all(), zero cost) on 2 of those absence units found the missing fact WAS present in the full store but outside the top-10, and a hand-written HyDE-style hypothetical query (not the literal question) moved it from absent to rank 1 in both cases -- a strong, confirmed, non-hypothetical precondition. Independent support: LongMemEval's own primary-source construction methodology (arXiv:2410.10813, appendix A.1) states evidence sessions are built to 'convey the evidence statement indirectly' rather than in the question's own words.
